relationships.subject: SMS1
relationships.evidence_quote: SMS1, localized to the trans-Golgi, generates DAG, which serves as a key signaling lipid required for PKD activation and efficient cargo export

relationships.subject: diacylglycerol
relationships.evidence_quote: This metabolic signaling generates a DAG pool that acts as a beacon, binding to the C1 domains of cytosolic protein kinase D (PKD) and recruiting it to the organelle

relationships.subject: CSF1
relationships.evidence_quote: Here, it binds to CSF1R, a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed almost exclusively by microglia in the CNS

key_findings: Hypothesis paper: SMS1-DAG-PKD signaling promotes Golgi-to-membrane trafficking of CSF1R in spinal microglia, amplifying neuropathic pain.
Proposes SMS1 inhibition as microglia-sparing alternative to CSF1R kinase inhibitors.
